new_entities.name: L-theanine alone
new_entities.description: Oral L-theanine supplementation taken without caffeine or other active compounds.

new_entities.name: Acute subjective anxiety
new_entities.description: Self-reported anxiety or stress symptoms measured over minutes to weeks after an intervention.

edges.population: healthy adults or stressed but non-psychiatric adult populations
edges.mechanism: L-theanine is proposed to modulate glutamatergic signaling and sympathetic arousal, which could reduce perceived tension in some settings. In human trials, however, that theoretical calming effect appears context-sensitive, with more consistent signals in stressed participants over days to weeks than in strong laboratory anxiety provocations.
edges.summary: L-theanine has a plausible but still modest human signal for reducing subjective stress and anxiety-related symptoms. The overall literature leans positive, especially in stressed populations, but the effect is not large and the evidence base is much thinner than supplement marketing often implies.
edges.caveats: The literature mixes short laboratory stress paradigms with multi-week supplementation studies, so not every trial is testing the same thing. Sample sizes are small, subjective scales vary between studies, and the real-world effect size is likely modest rather than dramatic.

evidence.citation: Williams JL et al 2020 Plant Foods Hum Nutr
